why: BMR-Review 1e0e7f5 (2026-11-11, operator ruling of that day; T48): EVERY same-type child pair without a common family is a family mismatch, including a pair whose Family IDs are unknown and whose parents differ. Before, the mismatch fired only when both families were known; with a family unknown the gate fell back to comparing parents. Two Episodes titled 'Pilot', same year, length and language, under different parents that are in-sheet Row IDs (deferred, so no Family ID can be known on either side): rejected. Pair of family-unknown-different-parents-identity-altid-review: a shared identity Alt ID is the one thing that surfaces such a pair, at Review. A case fixture, because the score is the same before and after 1e0e7f5 (an ineligible pair either way): what moved is that the pair is now a FAMILY MISMATCH, which the reason states ('no common Family ID') and which a shared identity Alt ID can surface; notes_match pins it.
